label: STOPP C10
title: NSAID with an anticoagulant
statement: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and vitamin K antagonist, direct thrombin inhibitor or factor Xa inhibitors in combination (risk of major gastrointestinal bleeding).

source.document: O'Mahony D, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632, Appendix 1 (corrected supplementary file; NHS Somerset copy used for text, sentence-identical to the earlier parse)
source.citation: O'Mahony D, Cherubini A, Guiteras AR, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632. doi:10.1007/s41999-023-00777-y

plain_summary: An anti-inflammatory pain medicine (NSAID) supplied together with a blood thinner such as warfarin, dabigatran, apixaban or rivaroxaban raises the risk of serious bleeding from the stomach or bowel.

medicine_groups.name: NSAIDs, the anti-inflammatory pain medicines

ibuprofen: Advil Childrens Pain and Fever 2 to 7 Years
Advil Childrens Pain and Fever 7 to 12 Years
Advil Childrens Pain and Fever Relief 2 to 12 Years
Advil Infants Pain and Fever Relief 3 Months to 2 Years
Nurofen for Children 3 Months to 5 Years

medicine_groups.note: Tablets, capsules, liquids, suppositories and injections count. Skin gels, creams and eye drops do not count, for example Voltaren Emulgel. Aspirin is not in this group. Nurofen Plus and Panafen Plus are ibuprofen with codeine. Nuromol and Maxigesic are ibuprofen with paracetamol. Arthrotec is diclofenac with misoprostol. Vimovo is naproxen with esomeprazole. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too.

medicine_groups.name: Warfarin, dabigatran and the factor Xa inhibitors
medicine_groups.note: Warfarin is the vitamin K antagonist. Dabigatran is the direct thrombin inhibitor. Apixaban, rivaroxaban, edoxaban and fondaparinux are factor Xa inhibitors. No Australian brand is listed for edoxaban. Fondaparinux is an injection. Heparin and enoxaparin are not in this group. Antiplatelet medicines such as aspirin and clopidogrel are not anticoagulants. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too.

rule_for_models: Apply this criterion only to people aged 65 years or older. For a person under 65, report no finding. If age is unknown and the other evidence would support a finding, report it only as possible and identify age as missing. Suspect a finding when at least one Group A medicine (an NSAID) AND at least one Group B medicine (warfarin, dabigatran, apixaban, rivaroxaban, edoxaban or fondaparinux) both appear in the history and their supply dates overlap or fall within 60 days of each other. One supply of each is enough.
cannot_be_seen: The reason for each prescription may be unknown. Check any recorded INR, kidney function results and history of stomach ulcer or bleeding. Tests or events outside this record may be missing. Also how often the NSAID is really taken, anti-inflammatory medicines bought without a prescription, and medicines supplied by a hospital or another pharmacy.
ask_the_gp: Whether the NSAID is still needed while the anticoagulant continues, and the patient's risk of bleeding.
